raw_case_text: A-82-year-old otherwise healthy male had a history of fever of 1 week. He was not a diabetic or hypertensive. There was no history of trauma. After few days, he developed headache with vomiting which was associated with low backache. This was followed with gradual onset of weakness of lower limbs and urinary incontinence. The weakness worsened over the next few days to flaccid paralysis in both lower limbs. He was taken to a local hospital from where he was referred to us. On examination, he was conscious but not oriented. There were patchy ecchymotic patches on his sacral region. GCS was E4V4M5 along with Grade 0 power of lower limbs. There was no perception of any sensations below the trunk. There was normal power in the upper limbs. Investigations revealed he had severe thrombocytopenia (platelet count 20,000/mm3) which prompted further evaluation for dengue in view of ongoing epidemic. He was positive for dengue IgM antibodies. His INR was 1.3 and APTT was 45 s. Emergency CT scan of the brain along with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the spine was advised. CT scan revealed diffuse patchy subarachnoid hemorrhages involving both cerebral hemispheres along with intraventricular bleed [Figure 12a and b]. MRI spine showed he had subdural and intramedullary hematoma involving the thoracolumbar region. The spinal cord was distended from T11 to L1 regions due to underlying hematoma [Figures 13 and 14]. It was decided to perform emergency decompression of the spinal cord, but his platelet counts were too low to perform a safe surgery. He was given multiple platelet transfusions after which thrombocytopenia slowly recovered partially to more than one lac over a period of 4 days after admission. He was taken up for surgery during which, a laminectomy of the T11, T12, and L1 vertebrae was performed. The cord was seen swollen with underlying bluish blush of the hematoma [Figure 15]. The dura was opened to visualize the underlying subdural clot which was removed slowly with biopsy forceps [Figure 16]. The hematoma was seen to enter the substance of the spinal cord and was splaying the nerve roots. Thorough irrigation with saline was given and the hematoma was evacuated in piecemeal. At the end of the surgery, the cord was seen pulsating after which a meticulous dural closure was achieved. He regained consciousness after surgery but the power in his lower limbs did not improve.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 82-year-old male presenting with a 1-week history of fever, headache, vomiting, low backache, progressive flaccid paraplegia, and urinary incontinence.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: An 82-year-old male presented with a 1-week history of fever, headache, and vomiting associated with lower back pain. Over the subsequent days, he developed progressive lower extremity weakness and urinary incontinence, rapidly worsening into complete flaccid paraplegia. He was referred to a tertiary neurosurgical center due to severe thrombocytopenia and acute paraplegia.
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously healthy. No history of diabetes mellitus, hypertension, or spinal trauma.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, headache, vomiting, severe backache, bilateral leg weakness, numbness below the waist, and urinary incontinence. Upper extremity function intact. Medications: none. Allergies: null.

objective.physical_examination: Conscious, disoriented (GCS E4V4M5 = 13/15). Skin: Patchy ecchymoses over the sacral region. Neurological examination: Complete flaccid paraplegia with muscle power grade 0/5 in bilateral lower extremities; normal motor power in bilateral upper extremities. Complete sensory loss (absent touch and pain perception) below the trunk. Autonomic: Urinary retention/incontinence.
objective.routine_investigations: Platelet count: 20,000/mm3, recovering to >100,000/mm3 over 4 days following multiple platelet transfusions. Coagulation profile: INR 1.3, aPTT 45 sec.
objective.advanced_workup: Brain CT: Diffuse patchy subarachnoid hemorrhage involving bilateral cerebral hemispheres along with intraventricular hemorrhage. Whole spine MRI: Subdural and intramedullary hematoma in the thoracolumbar region with spinal cord distension from T11 to L1. Operative findings: T11-L1 laminectomy revealed a swollen cord with bluish hematoma, subdural clot, and intramedullary clot splaying nerve roots.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Severe dengue infection complicated by multi-compartment central nervous system hemorrhages: spontaneous thoracolumbar subdural and intramedullary hematoma (T11-L1) causing complete spinal cord compression, intracranial subarachnoid hemorrhage, and intraventricular hemorrhage. Diagnostic confirmation: Positive dengue virus IgM antibodies in the setting of a regional dengue epidemic.
Plan & Outcome: Resuscitation with multiple platelet transfusions raising platelets above 100,000/mm3, followed by emergent T11, T12, and L1 decompressive laminectomy and microsurgical evacuation of subdural and intramedullary hematomas. Following surgery, consciousness normalized, but flaccid paraplegia remained unchanged.
